The FastAPI docs I found don't describe an "admin-only" setup specifically. The closest thing they cover is **OAuth2 scopes**, which give you fine-grained permissions you could use for this. This would allow you to have a more fine-grained permission system, following the OAuth2 standard, integrated into your OpenAPI application (and the API docs).[2]

**How the pieces fit together, according to the docs:**

- **Declare the required scopes with `Security`.** When you need to declare dependencies with OAuth2 scopes you use `Security()`.[4] By using `Security` instead of `Depends`, **FastAPI** will know that it can declare security scopes, use them internally, and document the API with OpenAPI.[3]
- **Read the scopes in your user dependency with `SecurityScopes`.** In your `get_current_user` dependency, you declare a special parameter of type `SecurityScopes`, imported from `fastapi.security`.[3]
- **Apply it per endpoint.** The same way you can define a `list` of `Depends` in the decorator's `dependencies` parameter, you could also use `Security` with `scopes` there.[5]
- **Enforce the check yourself.** You still enforce those scopes, or any other security/authorization requirement, however you need, in your code.[2]

The tools are imported from `fastapi.security`:

```python
from fastapi.security import OAuth2PasswordBearer, SecurityScopes
```

**Before you choose this approach:** You don't necessarily need OAuth2 scopes, and you can handle authentication and authorization however you want.[2] In many cases, OAuth2 with scopes can be an overkill.[2]

The excerpts I have don't include a complete code example for scope checks. The full walkthrough is at https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/advanced/security/oauth2-scopes/, and the security tools reference is at https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/reference/security/.
